steps.tx: The **pyruvate dehydrogenase complex** stands at the gate between cytosolic glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidation, decarboxylating pyruvate to acetyl-CoA with NADH and carbon dioxide released. Animals cannot reverse this step, so acetyl-CoA from fat or glucose can never rebuild glucose. That single irreversibility explains why fatty acids fail as glucose precursors while glycerol and odd chain fragments succeed.
steps.say: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex gates entry from glycolysis into mitochondrial oxidation, making acetyl-CoA with NADH and carbon dioxide. Animals cannot reverse this step, so acetyl-CoA can never rebuild glucose. That irreversibility explains why fatty acids fail as glucose precursors.

steps.tx: Three enzymes share the work inside one giant assembly: **E1** decarboxylates with thiamine pyrophosphate, E2 transfers the acetyl group to coenzyme A through a swinging lipoamide arm, and E3 restores the arm using FAD and NAD. Five coenzymes cooperate in sequence (thiamine, lipoic acid, coenzyme A, FAD, NAD), remembered as Tender Loving Care For Nancy.
steps.say: Three enzymes share the work. E1 decarboxylates with thiamine pyrophosphate, E2 transfers the acetyl group to coenzyme A through a swinging lipoamide arm, and E3 restores the arm using FAD and NAD. Five coenzymes cooperate: thiamine, lipoic acid, coenzyme A, FAD and NAD.

steps.tx: A dedicated kinase switches the complex off by phosphorylation when **NADH**, acetyl-CoA or ATP announce that energy is abundant. A phosphatase switches it back on when ADP, calcium or insulin request more oxidation, matching pyruvate burning to muscle contraction and feeding. Pyruvate itself restrains the kinase, so substrate arrival tends to open its own gate.
steps.say: A kinase switches the complex off when NADH, acetyl-CoA or ATP announce that energy is abundant. A phosphatase switches it back on when ADP, calcium or insulin request more oxidation. Pyruvate itself restrains the kinase, so substrate arrival opens its own gate.

steps.tx: Arsenite poisons the complex by gripping the sulfhydryl groups of **lipoic acid**, freezing the swinging arm mid cycle. Pyruvate and lactate then pile up while acetyl-CoA starves, producing vomiting, rice water stools, garlic scented breath and capillary leak in acute poisoning. The same chemistry disables alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, compounding energy failure in brain and gut.
steps.say: Arsenite grips the sulfhydryl groups of lipoic acid and freezes the swinging arm. Pyruvate and lactate pile up while acetyl-CoA starves, producing vomiting, rice water stools and garlic scented breath. The same chemistry disables alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

steps.tx: Thiamine deficiency disables the same gate from the coenzyme side, which is why giving glucose first can precipitate crisis. Glycolysis accelerates, pyruvate cannot pass, lactate climbs, and vulnerable brainstem nuclei fail as **Wernicke encephalopathy** with confusion, ataxia and eye movement palsies. Thiamine before glucose, generous magnesium replacement and slow refeeding prevent this predictable iatrogenic worsening.

steps.tx: Children born with a faulty complex present differently, with congenital **lactic acidosis**, hypotonia, seizures and developmental delay from the first months. Dichloroacetate can help by inhibiting the PDH kinase and holding residual enzyme in its active state, alongside a ketogenic strategy in selected cases. Distinguishing this neurology picture from pyruvate kinase haemolysis anchors the clinical lesson that follows.
steps.say: Children born with a faulty complex present with congenital lactic acidosis, hypotonia, seizures and developmental delay. Dichloroacetate inhibits the kinase and holds residual enzyme active. This neurology picture contrasts with the haemolysis of pyruvate kinase deficiency.
